title: Lesson 22 - You Might Want to Get That Checked

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Is your wrist bothering you again?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: A little. It's been sore for about ten days. It feels better in the morning, but it starts hurting after I work for an hour.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: You might want to get that checked.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I thought it might go away on its own.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: It might, but I can't tell what it is. Since it keeps happening, you should talk to a healthcare professional.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: That's fair. I have notes about when it starts and what makes it worse.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Good. It might be a good idea to bring those notes.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: The clinic's appointment line closes at five, and it's four forty-five now.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Then you'd better call before it closes, or you'll have to wait until tomorrow to schedule.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I'll call now. I'm not asking you to tell me what's wrong—I just needed a push to make the appointment.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Exactly. I can notice that the problem keeps returning, but I'm not qualified to diagnose it.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Thanks for keeping the advice practical.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: If you ever have an emergency warning sign, don't wait for a routine appointment—get urgent help.
